cards.title: Baseline change check
cards.summary: Focus on change from the person’s usual baseline and functional impact.
cards.when_to_use: Mood, anxiety, thought, sleep, or behavior changes.
steps: Ask what changed and when.
Check sleep, eating, self-care, work/school, relationships, and safety.
Ask about medication/substance changes.
Identify whether clinician contact is needed sooner.
cautions: Do not convert a checklist into a diagnosis.

cards.title: Medication question organizer
cards.summary: Prepare questions and observations for a prescriber/pharmacist without changing treatment.
cards.when_to_use: Side effects, adherence, missed doses, or uncertainty about psychiatric medication.
steps: Record medication name and prescribed instructions.
Record what changed and when.
List side effects/benefits and severity.
Note missed doses or substance/OTC changes.
Contact prescriber/pharmacist for dose/start/stop/taper decisions.
cautions: Possible overdose, severe reaction, dangerous withdrawal, or immediate medical danger requires urgent/emergency help.

cards.title: Sleep change escalation check
cards.summary: Treat major sleep change as clinically relevant context rather than only a sleep-hygiene problem.
cards.when_to_use: Marked reduction/increase in sleep with mood, energy, or thought changes.
steps: Record sleep amount and change from baseline.
Check energy, impulsivity, agitation, slowed behavior, and functioning.
Check medication/substance changes.
Contact a clinician if the change is marked, persistent, or concerning.

cards.title: Reality-oriented support
cards.summary: Support safety and reduce confrontation when someone reports unusual perceptions or beliefs.
cards.when_to_use: Possible hallucinations, paranoia, or difficulty distinguishing internal experience from external reality.
steps: Validate distress without confirming an unverified belief as fact.
Ask whether the experience is creating danger or commands to act.
Reduce stimulation and involve trusted support if wanted.
Encourage timely professional assessment, urgent if safety/function is deteriorating.
cautions: Do not ridicule, aggressively debate, or reinforce delusions as established fact.

cards.title: Panic support
cards.summary: Reduce secondary fear and orient to safety while keeping medical uncertainty in mind.
cards.when_to_use: Panic-like episodes when no emergency has been established.
steps: Check whether symptoms could need emergency medical evaluation, especially if new/severe.
Name the experience as intense and time-limited without guaranteeing the cause.
Use a tolerable grounding anchor.
Slow the next action and reduce stimulation.
Discuss recurrent episodes with a clinician.
cautions: Do not tell someone chest pain or breathing difficulty is definitely anxiety.

cards.title: Trauma-informed choice
cards.summary: Increase control and predictability rather than forcing disclosure.
cards.when_to_use: Trauma-related distress or when sensitive topics arise.
steps: Ask permission before detailed exploration.
Offer choices and explain why a question matters.
Allow stopping or changing topic.
Prioritize stabilization and safety.
Support connection to trauma-informed professional care when desired.
